title: Why You Jolt When Someone Gets Too Close
hook: You feel a jolt of alarm if someone gets too close to your face.

narration.text: You feel a jolt of alarm if someone gets too close to your face.
This is your personal space protection system.
Your brain monitors a bubble of space around you.
It extends about an arm's length in front.
When someone enters it, your amygdala, the brain's alarm bell, activates.
This creates the sudden feeling of unease or threat.
So, next time, notice that instinctive reaction, and like this if it surprised you, then subscribe for more insights into your amazing mind.

description: Ever wondered why you feel an instinctive jolt of discomfort when someone invades your personal space? It is not just politeness; your brain has a built-in alarm system to protect your personal bubble.
topic: Why you feel a jolt of alarm if someone unexpectedly gets too close to your face. This is your personal space protection.
